clue.text: One regularly dipping into float for money

definitions.text: One regularly dipping into float for money

parts.words: One regularly dipping into float for money
parts.note: surface reading: someone who keeps helping themselves to the cash float in a till
setter's reading: the float is the small electric delivery van this tradesman works from, dipping into it for each round's orders and getting paid for them

explanation.surface: A shop worker keeps skimming coins from the till's float.
explanation.walkthrough: A float is both the cash kept in a till for change and the slow electric van used for doorstep deliveries in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: This tradesman delivers bottles door to door from his float and collects payment from customers.

clue.text: Objects to film's world-view

parts.note: someone who minds something objects to it
E.T. is Spielberg's film about an extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: Someone dislikes a film's outlook on life.
explanation.definitionFit: A mindset is a person's settled attitude or outlook, their way of seeing things.

clue.text: Brood over deal ultimately getting smaller

indicators.note: in a down clue one thing over another covers it, wrapping around it

parts.note: a litter is a brood of young animals born together

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the last letter of the word before

parts.note: the last letter of deal

explanation.surface: Someone frets over a shrinking deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Brood looks like a verb for worrying; it is a noun for a set of young.
explanation.definitionFit: Littler is an informal comparative of little, meaning more small.

clue.text: Corporation upset with journalist being silenced

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a corporation is a jocular word for a large belly, a tum
ED is the usual abbreviation for an editor

explanation.surface: A corporation is upset at a journalist being gagged.
explanation.walkthrough: Corporation is old slang for a pot belly, not a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Muted describes something quietened or toned down, as though made silent.

clue.text: Reminiscent of losing act unfortunately

indicators.note: something that goes unfortunately goes wrong, so the letters fall out of order

parts.note: the nine letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A performer recalls an act that lost, sadly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nostalgic means looking back fondly and wistfully on the past.

clue.text: Did divine female ring and swear badly?

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters of the word beside it come out in a wrong order

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for female
a ring is the shape of the letter O
the five letters of swear rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman telling fortunes rings a client and curses clumsily, the question asking whether that counts as divination.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine the future is to predict it, and the past tense of foresee means predicted.

clue.text: Type of Ford Sierra belonging to retired copper originally

indicators.note: something retired has withdrawn, gone back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: of means belonging to, as in the house of my father
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
Sierra is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for S

explanation.surface: An old Ford Sierra once owned by a retired policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sierra was itself a Ford car, which makes the surface convincing; copper is the metal, not a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Focus is a family hatchback model made by Ford, so it names one kind of Ford car.

clue.text: Carpet salesman on edge with …

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
a rim is an edge
and means together with

explanation.surface: A carpet salesman on the edge of a sale, continued into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Carpet looks like a floor covering being sold; it is the verb meaning to scold.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is to call them in and scold them, a dated British idiom for a formal telling-off.

clue.text: … incentives for everyone (within fixed limits)

indicators.note: within puts the first piece inside the second
fixed in the sense of rigged or rearranged, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all audiences
the six letters of limits rearranged

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: rewards for all staff, kept within set bounds.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating for a film anyone may watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Stimuli are things that spur activity or effort, which is what incentives do.

clue.text: Success wrapping present in what?

indicators.note: wrapping something means going all round it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a win is a success
here is what you say to show you are present at a roll-call

explanation.surface: A successful gift-wrapping job, and someone asks what the present is wrapped in.
explanation.walkthrough: Present looks like a gift being wrapped; it means in attendance. The question mark makes the definition a question.
explanation.definitionFit: Wherein is the formal word meaning in which, or as a question, in what.

clue.text: Turning TV on to check darts — oddly missing scores

indicators.note: a check halts something in its middle, so these letters are lodged between the others
turning something round makes the whole string read from the other end

parts.note: a TV is a television set

indicators.note: with the odd-numbered letters gone, only the second, fourth and so on of the word before survive

parts.note: the even letters of darts
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone switches the television on to keep an eye on the darts, and some of the scores are lost along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of darts sit between the TV word and ON, and the whole run is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To score music is to write it out, and notates is the verb for recording it in musical notation.

clue.text: Picture moulding once hollow resin replaced by very soft wood

indicators.note: says one set of letters is taken out and a different set put in their place

parts.note: a cornice is the decorative moulding running round the top of a wall, where picture rails sit

indicators.note: a hollow word has had its insides scooped out, leaving only its two end letters

parts.note: the outside letters of resin, the pair that is swapped out
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft

explanation.surface: A craftsman's picture frame, once its resin filling is gone, gets patched with a very soft timber.
explanation.walkthrough: The RN in the middle of the moulding word is swapped for PP; 'once' just means 'when'.
explanation.definitionFit: A coppice is a small wood of trees regularly cut back to the stump so they regrow.

clue.text: Youth voices entertaining panto when in cast

indicators.note: a host entertaining guests has them inside, so one word holds the other

parts.note: to voice something is to say it

indicators.note: with 'in' cast off, those two letters are thrown out of the show's title

parts.note: Aladdin is one of the most popular Christmas pantomimes, the comic family musical plays staged every winter in Britain

explanation.surface: Young people in a pantomime cast are being entertained by voices.
explanation.walkthrough: Aladdin is a favourite Christmas pantomime, the comic family musical staged every winter in Britain; 'when in cast' means the show's title throws out IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Salad days, Shakespeare's phrase, means the inexperienced time of one's youth.

clue.text: Popular application's not free?

parts.note: something in is fashionable or popular
an application is a use something is put to

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a popular app is one you must pay for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' looks like it means costing nothing; the definition means unoccupied, like a toilet or a meeting room.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in use is occupied or engaged, so it is not available for anyone else.

clue.text: Confuse shy host

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to hurl, as at a coconut shy
third meaning: to hold a party

explanation.surface: A timid party host is flustered.
explanation.walkthrough: There are three separate meanings here; 'shy' and 'host' read as adjective and noun but are both verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to disconcert, to fling something, and to put on a party, as in throwing a bash.

clue.text: Persuading despicable sort to hide diamonds in part of plane

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it tucked inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: the wing is part of an aeroplane

indicators.note: in places the whole assembled piece inside the final one

parts.note: a heel is a contemptible man, a cad
D is the abbreviation for the card suit of diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone coaxes a villain into smuggling diamonds in an aircraft's wing.
explanation.walkthrough: This works like a set of nesting dolls: one container sits inside another. A heel is old-fashioned slang for a cad.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheedling is coaxing someone with flattery or sweet talk to get what one wants.

clue.text: Planning and finally swimming the channel

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of each of the two words that follow it

parts.note: the last letters of swimming and the
a TV or radio channel is a station

explanation.surface: Someone preparing at last to swim the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel looks like the sea crossing, but it is a broadcasting channel.
explanation.definitionFit: Gestation is the period over which a plan or idea is developed before it emerges, borrowed from pregnancy.

clue.text: For example, tee up following small drink

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the word before it is placed behind the abbreviation that comes next in the clue

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
taken as written
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: A golfer tees up after a quick drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts UP after the S; the definition is the golf tee, which props up the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf tee is a peg that holds the ball up off the ground, an example of something that props.

clue.text: Bloomer's flatter crust's initially boring

indicators.note: something boring drills into another thing, so it ends up inside it

parts.note: to butter up someone is to flatter them

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of the word before it is used

parts.note: the first letter of crust

explanation.surface: A baker's flat bloomer loaf has a dull crust.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is a British crusty loaf, which is the false scent; here it is something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is anything that flowers, and the buttercup is a common yellow wild flower.

clue.text: Jerk with ambition to be comedian

parts.note: to bob is to move with a quick jerk up and down
a hope is an ambition; with just joins the two parts

explanation.surface: An idiot who wants to become a stand-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Jerk reads as an insult; it is a quick movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Hope was a British-born American comic actor famous for his film and stage comedy.

clue.text: Peter Andre's beginning to get sloshed, quaffing butt of Shiraz in swingers' bar

indicators.note: quaffing means drinking down, so the other letters swallow this one
sloshed means drunk, and drunk letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a word's beginning is its opening letter only

parts.note: the first letter of Andre

indicators.note: the butt is the tail end, so the last letter of the wine word

parts.note: the last letter of Shiraz

explanation.surface: The pop singer Peter Andre gets drunk on red wine in a bar for swingers.
explanation.walkthrough: Swingers looks like partner-swapping; here they are trapeze artists swinging from a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze is a horizontal bar hung on ropes that circus acrobats swing on.

clue.text: Material this writer's daughter recalled

indicators.note: something recalled is called back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the setter, as this writer, says 'mine' for what belongs to them
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A writer remembers fabric from their daughter's childhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a hard-wearing cotton twill fabric used for jeans.

clue.text: Den's consuming snack most ordered

indicators.note: consuming means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a nest is an animal's den or lair
to snack is to eat, here in the past tense, since 'Den's consuming' reads as 'Den has consumed'

explanation.surface: Den, a man, is eating a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: Den looks like a man's name; it is a lair.
explanation.definitionFit: Neatest is the superlative of neat, meaning the tidiest or most orderly.

clue.text: Young man inspired by Madonna's craft

indicators.note: something inspired is breathed in, so this piece is drawn inside the other

parts.note: the Madonna is the Virgin Mary
a son is a young man of a family

explanation.surface: A young man takes inspiration from the pop singer Madonna's art.
explanation.walkthrough: Madonna points to the singer, but it is the Virgin Mary.
explanation.definitionFit: Masonry is the stonemason's skill of building with dressed stone, a trade or craft.

clue.text: Stole case of redwood timber

parts.note: a boa is a long scarf or stole of feathers or fur

indicators.note: the case is the outer shell, so only the outside letters of the following word are used

parts.note: the first and last letters of redwood

explanation.surface: Someone stole a crate of redwood.
explanation.walkthrough: Stole looks like the past of steal; it is the wrap worn round the shoulders.
explanation.definitionFit: A board is a flat cut length of wood, part of the timber trade.

clue.text: They vandalise iPhone essentially over poor signal

indicators.note: a poor version of a word is a corrupted one, its letters out of their proper order
the essence of a word is its core, so its central pair of letters is used

parts.note: the middle two letters of iPhone
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over
the six letters of signal rearranged

explanation.surface: Vandals smash phones, complaining about a weak signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooligans are violent, rowdy youths who cause damage to property.

clue.text: Timeless broadcast of The Kid had tramp

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered about, so the letters are spread into a new order
timeless means with the time symbol taken out

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A broadcast of the Chaplin film The Kid featured his tramp.
explanation.walkthrough: T, the physics symbol for time, leaves THE KID; The Kid is a Charlie Chaplin film, and his Tramp character adds to the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a tramp is to take a long walk, and hiked means walked far over country.

clue.text: Vegetarian somewhat flipping furious

indicators.note: flipping over means turning end to end, so the run of letters reads backwards
somewhat means only part of the word, a run of its letters

parts.note: a run of letters from the middle of the word

explanation.surface: A vegetarian is rather flipping furious.
explanation.walkthrough: Flipping reads as a mild British swear word meaning 'very'; here it is the turning indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means very angry, a close synonym of furious.

clue.text: Column that makes a point using corrupt principles of Sergeant Ernie Bilko

indicators.note: something corrupt is spoilt or distorted, so the letters are jumbled
principles here means the first or leading parts, so the opening letters of the two words that follow

parts.note: the first letters of Sergeant and Ernie
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sergeant Ernie Bilko, the scheming TV con-man, has questionable principles.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernie Bilko was the scheming army sergeant of the American TV comedy The Phil Silvers Show.
explanation.definitionFit: An obelisk is a tall stone pillar that tapers to a pyramid-shaped tip.

clue.text: Type of deal done working away during exercise

indicators.note: something happening during another thing falls within it

parts.note: to train is to exercise

indicators.note: away means sent off, so those letters leave the word they were part of

parts.note: taken as written
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A deal is struck while someone is away at the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing ON from DONE leaves DE, which goes into TRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade-in is a purchase where an old item is handed over as part payment for a new one.

clue.text: Came into view rolling back mile in 60 minutes

indicators.note: rolling back returns along the same path, so the letters are read from the end
in puts one item inside the other

parts.note: in angular measure sixty minutes make one degree
M is the abbreviation for mile

explanation.surface: Something rolled back a mile within an hour.
explanation.walkthrough: '60 minutes' suggests an hour, but here it is an angle: sixty minutes of arc make one degree.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to come out from somewhere and become visible.

clue.text: Engineers attempt to draw in space for part of astronaut's mission

indicators.note: drawing something in pulls it inside, so one piece goes into the middle of the other

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, followed by TRY for attempt
an en is a printer's space, half an em wide

explanation.surface: Engineers try to sketch something in space for an astronaut.
explanation.walkthrough: Space looks like outer space; it is the printer's en.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-entry is the return of a spacecraft into the Earth's atmosphere at the end of a flight.
